text:
The Rangers are losing games they control. Friday in Chicago they outshot the Blackhawks 26-9 with more than 12 minutes left, per Scott Powers of The Athletic, and still lost 2-1. That made it three straight losses, outscored 12-4, despite getting 51% of the expected goals in those games.

It is the season in miniature. New York is 13-11-1, but its process is among the East's better ones: 53.6% of the expected goals, 53% at five on five. The problem is finishing. The Rangers have scored about 12 fewer goals than their chances deserve, and our numbers say they have about three fewer points than they earned. Igor Shesterkin is doing his part, .926 with 4.0 goals saved above expected over his last four starts.

The injuries are piling up, which explains the trade for Max Sasson from Vancouver; the Rangers, per The Hockey News, expect him to make an instant impact. Pavel Dorofeyev went on injured reserve, and Yahoo reported Smits and Oliver Bjorkstrand out two to three months. That hurts most on the J.T. Miller line, where Dorofeyev and Tye Kartye had 64% of the expected goals. Sean Durzi is back after what he called a "frustrating" injury.

Our numbers give Mike Sullivan's team a 57% chance at the playoffs. What we'd watch: whether the Mika Zibanejad, Alexis Lafreniere and Gabe Perreault line keeps carrying even strength while the depth is patched, because the shots are there and the goals usually follow.
